runtimeAssumptions.runtimeV1Boundary: The first release is a single-machine, single-signing-identity, owner-operated CLI runtime for curated unmodified OpenVR/D3D11 games. It uses user-owned CrossOver, Steam, games, Apple tooling, and hardware; manually authored profiles; manual Vision Pro client launch; and the custom fake_openvr_real/openvr_submit_shim runtime rather than the real SteamVR compositor. Public distribution, OpenXR-only titles, direct Vulkan capture, other controllers, and automatic profile discovery are out of scope.
runtimeAssumptions.controlPlaneFoundation: Issue #60 provides artifact-aware doctor, a bounded detached host start supervisor, synchronized live status, and idempotent exact-owned stop commands. Start repeats exact sealed installed-layout admission under the fixed lifecycle lock, publishes idle only after stable launchd/Mach check-in and live signature identity, uses an identity-bound Unix control socket, and preserves foreign or unresponsive state rather than signaling cached PIDs. Stop and lifecycle quiescence authenticate schema-v2 owner, service, plist, bridge, and socket state without depending on the old artifact remaining available or matching the new checkout, so an installed update cannot deadlock behind its predecessor. Install and uninstall cooperatively stop that synchronized supervisor before acquiring the lifecycle lock. Game/profile ownership, Vision Pro waiting/connection transitions, streaming, and bounded recovery remain follow-up slices.
runtimeAssumptions.transactionFoundation: Issue #61 has a production-shaped lifecycle coordinator over the artifact planner and durable executor. The planner emits canonical directory-source digests and complete allowed-root authority; one fixed per-user lock, journal, history, and backup namespace is shared across checkouts and bindings; active work is quiesced, verified, recovered, or archived across direction changes; runtime-owned roots use private modes; content-namespaced stock backups are retained; recursive open-target and conservative per-filesystem capacity checks run before journal creation; and isolated fixtures cover commit, replay, uninstall, reinstall, crash recovery, locking, blockers, and CLI output. Issue #62's dev7 contract adds immutable unsealed and Developer ID sealed artifact stages: final readiness is derived from verified signed bytes, source/final tree provenance, exact authority/Team ID/bundle ID/CDHash, and a no-timestamp policy rather than manifest mode alone. Unsealed artifacts still return artifact.sealing_required before mutation. Probe 018 walks declared roots and target parents through no-follow descriptors, records parent identities in journal schema v2, and publishes ordinary file/tree changes through verified exclusive sibling moves. Probe 019's dev8 contract fixes the bridge URL, admits a prior tree only after marker and Developer ID policy validation, atomically exchanges existing stable bundles with Darwin/Linux descriptor primitives, requires the exact current tree to remain on uninstall, and normalizes only owner write/execute bits on exact journaled cleanup directories. A qualified prior-version migration, baseline restoration, and three further physical install/uninstall cycles now pass with the exact bridge retained, every non-anchor operation ready, and no cleanup, rollback, quarantine, undo, owner, or service residue. Lifecycle quiescence removes ordinary game/runtime writers; the JSON journal, final POSIX unlink interval, and orchestrated same-UID path swaps during external codesign inspection remain outside the authentication boundary against an intentionally hostile owner process. Game launch still waits on the bounded start supervisor and stable Launch Services/Local Network lifecycle gates.
runtimeAssumptions.secondTitleGeneralityGate: The Lab build 7242747 now produces visible eye imagery through the packaged D3D11/OpenVR path. Exact IVRInput_007 support removes the black submitted-resource blocker, and same-texture eye bounds now propagate into border-clamped Vulkan blits. Two consecutive post-merge runs of the sealed dev5 artifact passed 5,400 disconnected frames with visible-content validation at 89.817 and 90.006 FPS steady tails, zero producer/native drops, and zero pose gaps. Separately, an earlier source-backed physical candidate was user-confirmed clear. The gate remains open until PS VR2 Sense gameplay and at least 89.5 FPS physical steady-tail cadence pass together; direct Vulkan capture, a real SteamVR compositor, game binary changes, maintained game forks, and anti-cheat bypasses remain hard cut lines.
runtimeAssumptions.gameplayControllers: PS VR2 Sense controllers paired directly to Apple Vision Pro with visionOS 26-or-newer accessory tracking and the ALVR PSVR2Sense profile; the qualified device runs visionOS 27.0 beta
runtimeAssumptions.freedomSourceGeometry: Freedom can switch its submitted side-by-side texture from 3240x1800 to 2808x1560 at level load; the native IOSurface pool remains fixed at 3240x1800 and the focused gate expects that transition explicitly
runtimeAssumptions.crossoverBottleWarmup: The probe owns and resets the dedicated Steam bottle, atomically installs the patched MoltenVK with its existing signature, preloads that exact file in x86_64 mode, and keeps a small patched-library Notepad window open so the tested game is never the bottle's first GUI process; the initial producer handshake allows 600 seconds while per-frame gates remain unchanged
runtimeAssumptions.openBrushRuntimeDiscovery: Steam build 23545184 and current Open Brush desktop releases are OpenXR-only, so the compatibility probe pins official release 1.0.28, the newest verified OpenVR build. Physical immersive testing passes both PS VR2 Sense controller sources and all exercised Open Brush inputs, with exact pose pairing, hardware encode, UDP delivery, and decoder submission verified. Those worn runs occurred before the buffered-logger fix and showed low cadence; physical smoothness has not been requalified. The maintained launcher uses a 1280x720 mirror, 1080x1344 per-eye targets, and suppresses the broken animated-logo video during each run. The apparent 34 FPS source ceiling was a probe observer effect: the fake OpenVR runtime opened and closed its diagnostic file for every logged API call. A resolution-matched run of the SteamVR Tutorial binary through the custom OpenVR shim reproduced 31.192 FPS before that logger was corrected and retained the expected RGBA native-format failure. The runtime now keeps one locked buffered log file and preserves the same diagnostics. Extended disconnected Open Brush artifact real-native-encode-20260716T112248Z submitted, encoded, and released 5400/5400 frames with zero producer or native drops, a 90.006 FPS final window, 449 us average native conversion, and clean restoration. Hardened Tutorial artifact real-native-encode-20260716T113326Z records a target-specific cadence pass and 90.000 FPS tail while preserving its expected RGBA native-format failure. Official Freedom artifact real-native-encode-20260716T112715Z independently passed 5400/5400 disconnected frames with zero drops and a 90.006 FPS tail. Custom game builds and maintained game forks remain out of scope. Open Brush has completed its controller and performance-discriminator purpose.
runtimeAssumptions.freedomPhysicalLifecycle: Official Freedom physical artifact real-native-encode-20260716T132419Z passed initial viewing, Digital Crown recenter, headset removal/reentry, and full ALVR client termination/relaunch with a clear and smooth image. Longer soak artifact real-native-encode-20260716T152355Z then encoded and transported 81000/81000 target frames, held a 90.006 FPS final window, averaged 734 us native conversion, exhausted no native pool, and remained clear and smooth throughout approximately 15 minutes. After the finite host stopped, ALVR returned to search. Without a manual client relaunch, recovery artifact real-native-encode-20260716T154756Z created new stream and format epochs and encoded and transported 2700/2700 frames; the user looked after that short stream ended, so active recovery is machine-verified but not directly human-observed. A preceding cold Invalid Resource submission failed before any frame and did not reproduce on the immediate retry. AVP validation issue #41 is complete.
runtimeAssumptions.ciActionlint: Repo Hygiene runs actionlint v1.7.12 directly through Go with read-only contents permission. The lint gate does not depend on authenticated pull-request diff or GitHub Checks APIs, so transient identity-endpoint failures cannot replace the actionlint result.
runtimeAssumptions.iosurfaceLaunchdService: The native bridge claims fixed per-user Mach service com.alvr.macos-bridge.iosurface with bootstrap_check_in, authenticates raw Mach senders from kernel audit trailers, validates send-once reply rights, and drains oversized or invalid messages. The runner uses one global run lock and transient stable-path launchd plist, removes an owned stale job before replacing the signed app, requires one Launch Services record for the already-authorized app URL, verifies the expected Developer ID team and CDHash against the live launchd PID, signals through launchctl rather than cached PIDs, and fails if the job, plist, lock, client, or staged game files remain. Physical preflight now selects exactly one connected and unlocked Vision Pro, captures the exact launched PID before mDNS readiness, relaunches the installed ALVR client console-attached, parses its mDNS protocol/device ID/IP, and seeds that exact trusted identity before host startup. A producer startup barrier, first-frame prime, and bounded 100 ms slot wait prevent pre-ready traffic and transient producer loss. Connected artifact real-native-encode-20260716T223050Z passes the strict gate with 5400/5400 frames encoded and transported at 2880x1792, a 12 ms sink connection, zero producer/native drops, zero pose-generation gaps, one 5539 us backpressure wait, an 89.819 FPS full-run average, a 90.033 FPS tail, zero stale post-host IPD/origin/format diagnostics, and clean restoration. Post-review artifact real-native-encode-20260716T224204Z passes 30/30 while additionally proving exact Launch Services, live process identity, and global lock/plist/service teardown. Eyes-on artifact real-native-encode-20260716T230058Z again transported 5400/5400 frames with zero drops or pose gaps and a user-confirmed clear, smooth image; its cadence-only failure was caused by an unrelated concurrent nine-core FFmpeg AV1 probe plus other active host workloads, so it does not replace the strict automated pass. Final review-fix artifact real-native-encode-20260716T231338Z passes 30/30 with connection timing started at producer handshake, exact PID checks before and after post-host observation, synchronized stream-state diagnostics, zero stale messages, and exact teardown. The earlier discovery/cadence failure is superseded. This is the frozen transport and lifecycle baseline for issue #56; later runtime extraction may wrap it but may not weaken its identity, cadence, recovery, or teardown gates.

runtimeControl.boundary: Host-only start reaches synchronized idle after exact sealed install admission, a stable launchd PID/run/plist/program identity, live Developer ID verification, and a fresh bridge check-in marker. It owns one private generation directory and identity-bound Unix socket; stop is cooperative, exact, and remains available across prior-artifact contract drift. Game, profile, Vision Pro client, and streaming/recovery transitions remain next.

runtimeTransaction.boundary: Reusable journal-v2 transaction executor with exact planner tree identity, descriptor-pinned roots/parents, exclusive no-replace sibling publication, atomic stable-tree exchange, parent-drift recovery refusal, post-displacement removal verification, and per-entry journaled cleanup manifests; unsealed artifacts remain fail-closed, while sealed dev8 migration and three physical exact-restoration cycles are qualified before start/privacy integration

runtimeDescriptor.boundary: No-follow descriptor traversal, same-device descendants, exact descriptor hashing/copy, private directory creation, descendant-cache invalidation, and Darwin/Linux exclusive rename plus atomic exchange with no pathname fallback
